source_text: ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΠΕΡΙ ΕΛΕΟΥΣ ΚΑΙ ΚΡΙΣΕΩΣ. Πάτερ, εὐλόγησον. Ὁ μὲν ἐπιλανθανόμενος τοῦ Θεοῦ κόσμος, ἀδελ φοὶ, ἀδικίᾳ τῇ πρὸς τὸν πλησίον, καὶ ἀπανθρωπίᾳ τῇ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδυνάτους κρατεῖται, καθά περ ὁ θεῖος Ἀπόστολος λέγει, ὅτι Καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν Θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Θεὸς εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα, πεπληρωμένους πάσῃ ἀδικίᾳ, πονηρίᾳ, πλεονεξίᾳ, κακίᾳ, μεστοὺς φθόνου, φόνου, ἔριδος, δόλου, κακοηθείας, ψιθυριστὰς, καταλάλους, θεοστυγεῖς, ὑβριστὰς, ὑπερηφάνους, ἀλαζόνας, ἐφευρετὰς κακῶν, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς, ἀσυνέτους, ἀστόργους, ἀνελεήμονας· οὓς δὲ εἰς θεοσέβειαν ἐπανάγει Θεὸς, διδάσκει καὶ τὴν τῶν κακῶν ἀποχὴν καὶ τὴν τοῦ ἐλέους πρὸς τὸν πλησίον ἐπιμέ λειαν· ὥσπερ ὁ προφήτης ἐδίδαξεν Ἡσαΐας ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ Θεοῦ λέγων· Παύσασθε ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν, μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν. Καὶ εἶχεν ὁ νόμος πολλὰ μὲν προστάγματα περὶ τοῦ μὴ βλά πτειν τὸν πλησίον, ἐντολὰς δὲ καὶ περὶ τοῦ φιλανθρωπεύεσθαι καὶ ἐλεεῖν. Εἰ γάρ τις τὸ ἕτερον τούτων καταλίποι, θάτερον οὐχ ἱκανὸν εἰς διόρθωσιν ἀνθρώπου. Οὔτε γὰρ ἐξ ἀδίκων κερδῶν εὐεργεσία πρὸς τὸν δεόμενον δεκτὴ παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ, οὔτε ὁ τῶν ἀδικιῶν ἀπεχόμενος ἐπαινετὸς, εἰ μηδενὶ μεταδοίη τῶν ἑαυτοῦ. Περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῶν ἀδικούντων καὶ δῶρα Θεῷ προσφέρειν ἐπιχειρούντων γέγραπται· Θυσία ἀσεβῶν βδέλυγμα Κυρίῳ· περὶ δὲ τῶν μὴ ἐλεούντων· Ὁ φράσσων τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ τοῦ μὴ εἰσακοῦσαι πένητος, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπικαλέσεται, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ἐπακούων. Διὰ τοῦτο ἡ Παροιμία συμ βουλεύει· Τίμα τὸν Κύριον ἀπὸ σῶν δικαίων πό νων, καὶ ἀπάρχου αὐτῷ ἀπὸ σῶν καρπῶν δικαιο σύνης. Εἰ γὰρ ἐξ ἀδικίας καὶ ἁρπαγῆς μέλλεις προσφέρειν τῷ Θεῷ, κάλλιον μήτε κτήσασθαι τὴν τοιαύτην κτῆσιν, μήτε προσφέρειν ἐξ αὐτῆς. Καθα ρὸν γὰρ δῶρον ἀνοίσει τὴν εὐχὴν, ὡς γέγραπται· Εὐχαὶ κατευθυνόντων δεκταὶ παρ' αὐτῷ. Καὶ πά λιν, εἰ κτώμενος ἐκ δικαίων πόνων μὴ προσφέρεις Θεῷ προσφορὰς, ἀφ' ὧν τρέφονται πένητες, ἁρπαγὴ λογισθήσεταί σοι καθά φησι διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Μαλαχίου, ὅτι Αἱ ἀπαρχαὶ καὶ τὰ ἐπιδέκατα μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰσι, καὶ ἔσται ἡ διαρπαγὴ ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις ὑμῶν. Δεῖ τοίνυν, ἔλεον καὶ κρίσιν συγκεράσαντας ὑμᾶς, κτᾶσθαι μὲν μετὰ κρίσεως, ἀναλίσκειν δὲ εἰς ἔλεον, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἔλεον καὶ κρῖμα φυλάσσου, καὶ ἔγγιζε πρὸς Θεόν σου διαπαντός. Ἐλεημοσύνην γὰρ καὶ κρίσιν ἀγαπᾷ ὁ Θεός. Διόπερ ἐγγίζει πρὸς Θεὸν ὁ τοῦ ἐλέους καὶ τῆς κρίσεως προνοούμενος. Λοιπὸν ἐνταῦθα ἐξεταζέτω τις ἑαυ τὸν, καὶ σκοπείτω τοὺς ἰδίους πόρους ὁ πλού σιος, ἐξ ὧν ἀναφέρειν δῶρα μέλλει Θεῷ· μὴ τὸν πέ νητα κατεδυνάστευσε, μὴ τὸν ἀσθενέστερον ἐβιάσατο, μὴ τὸν ὑποκείμενον αὐτῷ πεπλεονέκτηκεν, ἐξουσίᾳ χρώμενος ἀντὶ δικαιοσύνης. Τὸ δίκαιον γὰρ καὶ τὴν ἰσό τητα κελευόμεθα φυλάττειν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς δούλους. Μὴ γὰρ, ὅτι κρατεῖς, βιάζου, μηδὲ, ὅτι δύνασαι, πλεονέκτει· ἀλλ' ὅτι πάρεστί σοι τὰ τῆς ἐξουσίας, δεῖξον τὰ τῆς δι καιοσύνης. Οὐ γὰρ ἐν ᾧ μὴ δύνασαι, παρέξεις τὴν ἀπόδειξιν τῆς πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ὑπακοῆς καὶ τοῦ φόβου, ἀλλ' ἐν ᾧ παραβῆναι δυνάμενος, οὐ παραβαίνεις.
thought_title: Mercy and justice must be joined
orientation: Basil opens the homily by describing the world that forgets God, then teaches that God requires both abstaining from harm and showing mercy, and that offerings must come from just gains.
pass_a_gloss: The world that forgets God, brothers, is ruled by injustice toward the neighbor and inhumanity toward the weak, just as the divine Apostle says, that 'As they did not see fit to have God in knowledge, God handed them over to a debased mind, to do the things that are not fitting, filled with all injustice, wickedness, greed, malice, full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, ill-nature, whisperers, slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, boasters, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents, without understanding, without natural affection, without mercy.' But those whom God leads up to godliness, he teaches both the abstaining from evils and the care of mercy toward the neighbor; just as the prophet Isaiah taught, speaking from the person of God: 'Cease from your wickednesses, learn to do good.' And the law had many commandments about not harming the neighbor, and also commands about being kind and showing mercy. For if someone leaves aside the one of these, the other is not sufficient for the correction of a person. For neither is a good deed from unjust gains toward the one in need acceptable to God, nor is the one abstaining from injustices praiseworthy, if he shares nothing of his own things with anyone. For concerning those who do injustice and attempt to offer gifts to God it is written: 'The sacrifice of the impious is an abomination to the Lord'; and concerning those who do not show mercy: 'The one who shuts his ears so as not to listen to the poor, he himself will call, and there will be no one listening.' Therefore the Proverb advises: 'Honor the Lord from your just labors, and offer first-fruits to him from your fruits of righteousness.' For if from injustice and robbery you are about to offer to God, it is better neither to have acquired such a possession, nor to offer from it. For a pure gift will bring up the prayer, as it is written: 'The prayers of the upright are acceptable with him.' And again, if while acquiring from just labors you do not offer to God offerings, from which the poor are fed, it will be reckoned to you as robbery, as he says through the prophet Malachi, that 'The first-fruits and the tithes are with you, and the plunder will be in your houses.' It is necessary therefore, having mixed mercy and justice, for you to acquire with justice, and to spend for mercy, according to what is written: 'Keep mercy and judgment, and draw near to your God always.' For God loves almsgiving and justice. Therefore the one who takes thought for mercy and justice draws near to God. For the rest, here let each person examine himself, and let the rich person consider his own sources of income, from which he is about to bring gifts to God: whether he has oppressed the poor person, whether he has used force against the weaker, whether he has exploited the one subject to him, using authority instead of justice. For we are commanded to keep what is just and fairness even toward slaves. For do not, because you have power, use force, nor, because you are able, exploit; but because the things of authority are present to you, show the things of justice. For not in what you cannot do will you provide the demonstration of obedience to God and of fear, but in what, being able to transgress, you do not transgress.

choices.why: The glossary bans 'humanity' for φιλανθρωπία; 'inhumanity' preserves the negative prefix and the contrast with kindness toward the weak.
Standard rendering of Romans 1:28; 'debased' captures the sense of failing the test, rejected by God.
The glossary maps φιλανθρωπία to 'kindness'; the verbal form is rendered as 'being kind' to keep the glossary term.

choices.english: it will be reckoned to you as robbery
choices.why: The glossary maps ἁρπαγή to 'robbery'; the passive of λογίζομαι is rendered 'will be reckoned' to preserve the accounting metaphor.
rejected: it will be counted as plunder

choices.why: The glossary maps ἰσότης to 'fairness'; used here for equal treatment even of slaves.
The glossary maps πλεονεξία to 'greed'; the imperative verb is rendered 'exploit' to capture the active taking of unjust advantage.

pass_b_english: Brothers, the world that forgets God is ruled by injustice toward its neighbor and inhumanity toward the weak. As the divine Apostle says: “Since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do what is not fitting. They were filled with every kind of injustice, wickedness, greed, and malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and evil-mindedness; whisperers, slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, boasters, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents, foolish, without natural affection, without mercy” (Romans 1:28-31). But those whom God leads back to godliness he teaches both to abstain from evil and to care for mercy toward their neighbor. So the prophet Isaiah taught, speaking from the person of God: “Stop your evil deeds; learn to do good” (Isaiah 1:16-17). The law had many commands about not harming one's neighbor, and also commands about being kind and showing mercy. If someone abandons one of these, the other is not enough to set a person right. For neither is a good deed to the needy from unjust gains acceptable to God, nor is the one who abstains from injustice praiseworthy if he shares nothing of his own. About those who commit injustice and still try to bring gifts to God it is written: “The sacrifice of the ungodly is an abomination to the Lord” (Proverbs 15:8). And about those who show no mercy: “Whoever shuts his ears so as not to hear the poor, he also will call out and there will be no one to listen” (Proverbs 21:13). Therefore the Proverb advises: “Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer him firstfruits from your fruits of righteousness” (Proverbs 3:9). For if you are about to bring an offering to God from injustice and robbery, it is better neither to acquire such a possession nor to bring an offering from it. For a pure gift will carry the prayer, as it is written: “The prayers of the upright are acceptable to him” (Proverbs 15:8). And again, if you acquire from righteous labors but do not bring offerings to God from which the poor are fed, it will be reckoned to you as robbery. So he says through the prophet Malachi: “The firstfruits and the tithes are with you, and the plunder will be in your houses” (Malachi 3:8-10). Therefore you must mix mercy and justice together: acquire with justice, and spend for mercy, according to what is written: “Keep mercy and justice, and draw near to your God always” (Hosea 12:6). For God loves almsgiving and justice (Psalm 33:5). So the one who attends to mercy and justice draws near to God. From here on, let each person examine himself, and let the rich person look at his own sources of income from which he is about to bring gifts to God: Did he oppress the poor? Did he force the weaker? Did he exploit the one under his authority, using power instead of justice? For we are commanded to keep what is just and fair even toward slaves. Do not use force just because you have power, and do not exploit just because you are able. Rather, since the means of authority are available to you, show the deeds of justice. For you will not give proof of your obedience to God and your fear of him in what you cannot do, but in what you are able to transgress and do not transgress.

fixed.note: The quote joins 3:8 (tithes and firstfruits are with you) and 3:10 (the plunder in the house), so the range should be 3:8-10, not 3:8-9 or 3:10 alone.

dismissed.why: Proverbs 15:8 is about sacrifice, not prayers of upright; prayers quote is Proverbs 15:29.
dismissed.note: LXX Proverbs 15:8 reads 'θυσίαι ἀσεβῶν βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ, εὐχαὶ δὲ κατευθυνόντων δεκταὶ παρ' αὐτῷ', so 15:8 is correct and 15:29 is a different line.
